notes: Two federates enter a single federation save/restore with different pending time roles: one regulator has Enable Time Regulation pending and one member has Enable Time Constrained pending. Both callbacks remain gated until after restore. The test proves that each callback is delivered exactly once to its originating federate ambassador, that pumping one evoked ambassador does not deliver the other member's callback, and that each member receives its own Federation Saved and Federation Restored callbacks. Fresh focused installed-package C++ CTest passed primary/contract in both callback models (4/4), supplementing recorded integer64/float64 C++ runs. Java compiled against the API-only JAR and passed focused packaged Umbra JNI runs in both callback models with both HLAinteger64Time and HLAfloat64Time: out/java-tck/restore-mixed-pending-time-role-evoked-jni-20261021.json, restore-mixed-pending-time-role-immediate-jni-20261021.json, restore-mixed-pending-time-role-float64-evoked-jni-20261021.json, and restore-mixed-pending-time-role-float64-immediate-jni-20261021.json. This focused slice does not establish process-restart persistence, transport interoperability, other Java providers, the full logical-time matrix, or conformance.
